analysis.title: Tesla, Inc. TSLA and SPCX Form Committees to Evaluate Potential Merger
key_insights: Musk said on the SpaceX Q3/26 earnings call that both SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees of independent directors to evaluate a merger at shareholders' request. Musk is a conflicted party and cannot take part in the committee discussions.
Musk pushed back on the idea that a merger is certain, while personally supporting it. He said the committees have not agreed on terms and there is no guarantee they will.
A transaction would need a 50% vote of all Tesla shares outstanding, not just those voting. Musk called this 'quite a high hurdle'.
Musk cited synergies in superintelligence software, chip design, Terafab, robotics and connectivity.
RBC thinks SPCX may need to pay a meaningful premium for TSLA shares. Musk controls about 20% of Tesla's voting power versus about 82% at SpaceX, which creates an asymmetric governance dynamic.

RBC believes TSLA holders would be receptive at $480 per share, which is its SOTP intrinsic value plus a roughly 15% premium. At current prices that implies an approximately 50/50 ownership split of the combined entity.

SpaceX is about 70% of RBC's combined pro forma valuation. SPCX holders could contribute most of the value while owning less than half of the combined company at $480 per share, which could draw pushback.

RBC sees Terafab, a joint chip manufacturing facility, as perhaps the most compelling near-term catalyst. It could remove duplicated R&D and unlock well over $1T in long-term cost savings versus sourcing chips externally, per RBC estimates.
RBC expects further commentary on the TSLA Q3/26 earnings call on Oct 21 at 5:30pm ET.

market_movers.rationale: The $480 target is a SOTP value that includes a roughly 15% premium for a potential SpaceX acquisition. The stock was at $373.71 at the prior close.
The target applies a weighted average 14.9x EV/EBITDA to 2029E EBITDA of $193.4B. The stock was at $147.79.

earnings_insights: SpaceX Q3/26 earnings call took place before this note, where Musk discussed the merger committees. The note gives no reported EPS or revenue figures.
TSLA Q3/26 earnings call is scheduled for Oct 21 at 5:30pm ET, and RBC expects more merger commentary then.
risk_factors: Musk said the merger is not certain and the special committees have not agreed on terms.
The 50% vote of all Tesla shares outstanding is a high approval hurdle.
SPCX shareholders could push back on owning less than half of the combined company while contributing about 70% of the value.

SpaceX risks include Starship development, launch failures, regulatory and licensing, orbital collision risk, early-stage loss-making xAI integration, key-person dependency on Musk, concentrated voting control, and AI capital intensity.
Tesla risks include lumpy quarterly results, cost headwinds, competition, regulatory risk, supply-chain inefficiencies and cyclical auto demand.

tension_points.bull_case: TSLA holders would be receptive at $480 per share, which is RBC's SOTP value plus a roughly 15% premium. Synergies include Terafab, which RBC says could save well over $1T versus sourcing chips externally.
tension_points.bear_case: SpaceX is about 70% of the combined pro forma valuation, so SPCX holders could own less than half the company at $480 and push back. Musk also called the 50% vote of all Tesla shares outstanding a high hurdle.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The special committees fail to agree on terms, or the deal fails to win a 50% vote of all Tesla shares outstanding.
